I have been farming these 12 mu in Quzhou for 45 years, and finishing high school means I don't just do what my father did — I think about the soil balance and whether I'm getting my money back on every jin of fertilizer. At 62, with only my wife and me working, I have to be careful with cash, but I also know that cutting inputs too close is gambling with the harvest. I would rather waste a little fertilizer than face a disaster.

My land is split: 8 mu in wheat-maize double cropping, which is my stable grain base, and 4 mu in cotton for cash. The wheat went in last October — I used an improved semi-dwarf variety and rotary tilled before sowing to break up the maize stubble without burying it too deep. For that 8 mu of wheat, I put down compound fertilizer as basal and will topdress urea at jointing. I figure the soil needs about 20 kg of pure nitrogen per mu to push toward 500 kg/mu, plus 8 kg of phosphorus and 5 kg of potassium to keep the nutrient balance after years of double cropping. I irrigate four times from the well: establishment, overwintering protection, jointing, and grain filling. The electricity bill hurts, but drought in May is my biggest enemy. I'll spray three times — herbicide at tillering and insecticide twice if aphids show up.

For summer maize, the window after wheat harvest is barely a week, so there is no time to plough. I will direct-seed a hybrid like Denghai or Nongda with no-tillage — the seed dealer says these hybrids can handle it, and my neighbor got 600 kg/mu last year doing the same. I budget 18 kg N per mu, with 5 kg P and 4 kg K from compound at planting, then side-dress urea when the plants are knee-high. Two irrigations: one if June is dry at planting, and one critical one at tasseling. Three pesticide applications total — herbicide once, then insecticide as needed.

The 4 mu of cotton I will plant in late April with an improved variety. Cotton is a money crop but it drinks pesticide. I plan 16 kg N, 6 kg P, and 7 kg K per mu because cotton is hungry for potassium at flowering. Rotary tillage before planting to warm the soil. I will irrigate three times — emergence, flowering, and boll setting — and spray 10 times through the season for bollworm, aphids, and weeds. It costs me over 600 yuan in chemicals for that 4 mu, but if I skip even one spray the bollworms will ruin everything. I expect about 300 kg/mu of seed cotton if the weather cooperates.

Everything ties to my pocket. If fertilizer prices jump, I might pull 2 kg of N back from the maize, but I won't touch the cotton pesticide budget — that is non-negotiable.
